newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges laid-off workers to look for new jobs.
newsitem.headline: China urges laid-off workers to look for new jobs.

text.p: China has told its millions of laid off workers to go out and find new jobs and not wait for the state to find work for them.
They also needed to lower their lofty expectations if they wanted to find employment, the official Workers' Daily said on Friday.

"Some laid-off workers just sit around waiting for higher authorities to arrange a new job for them instead of going out into the marketplace and seeking work themselves," the newspaper said in a front-page commentary.
Some even preferred to sit home on state relief rather than work as a private entrepreneur, it said, adding there was no shame in hourly work or running a street stall.
China once offered its workers what was known as the "iron ricebowl" -- lifetime employment at state companies that made few demands with barely a passing thought to productivity or profits.
But market-style reforms have spurred many of the nation's state companies to trim their bloated workforces or face bankruptcy.
The ranks of China's urban jobless are expected to swell to 5.9 million by the end of this year from 5.3 million at the end of March, the official media said last week.
Millions more have been sent home on a fraction of their pay due to economic difficulties, though they are not counted among the unemployed.
